reference: Parser contracts use the documented decimal value/PID grammar and preflight min<=max rule. Three reference adapters reject fixed malformed tokens independently, then retain original GNU file-operation/tree comparisons as auxiliary fixture coverage. Scheduler operations remain deferred. The redirected regular-file system model has independent fixed contents and is a custom contract, not util-linux system-sysctl parity.
coverage: Parser rejection for malformed clamp/PID, out-of-range value and reversed min/max before scheduler access.
Bash metadata; auxiliary ordinary file operations compared with GNU without counting them as scheduler coverage.
Actual private regular-file system-mode model: query, paired update, -1 keep-current and exact resulting file bytes.
exclusions: Live scheduler queries/changes, all-task execution, live system sysctls and child command mode remain deferred. Parser rejection and the documented private regular-file root seam are exercised without scheduler syscalls or live sysctl access.
No live procfs sysctl, scheduler attribute, host task, privilege, hardware, or network behavior is exercised.
No GNU uclampset CLI exists; the util-linux command is not presented as GNU parity.

cases.purpose: Compare assigned uclampset parser rejection before any scheduler access via a documented-grammar reference adapter, followed by the original private GNU file-operation comparison.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t uclampset) == builtin ]]; then
 if uclampset -m bad; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
else
 # Independent documented decimal grammar rejects this input before scheduler access.
 printf 'invalid clamp or PID argument\n' >&2
 rc=1
fi
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'parser-status=%s\n' "$rc"
mkdir -p 'fixture dir/sub'
touch 'fixture dir/sub/empty file'
chmod 640 'fixture dir/sub/empty file'
printf '%s\n' 'fixture ready'

cases.purpose: Check the Bash type builtin's documented -t result for a registered builtin without invoking uclampset.
Check that Bash help finds the uclampset documentation registered in the pinned source and emits nonempty metadata, without invoking the loadable operation.
cases.script: help uclampset > help.txt && [[ -s help.txt ]] && printf '%s\n' 'help available'

cases.purpose: Reject an explicit reversed clamp pair before any target read or mutation.
Check query formatting for one task and task enumeration with -a, without changing scheduler state.
cases.reason: Future run needs a disposable Linux VM with a controlled owned process and known thread set, plus an independent sched_getattr oracle for each TID. Verify PID 0 handling, comm fallback, output values, and that querying makes no scheduler writes. Do not use a host task.

cases.purpose: Check one-sided and paired clamp updates, reset values, -R, and preservation of unrelated scheduler attributes.
cases.reason: Future run needs a disposable VM with CONFIG_UCLAMP_TASK or a reviewed sched_getattr/sched_setattr mock that records request bytes and can inject kernel errors. Use an owned test process and an independent syscall oracle; assert policy, nice, priority, and deadline parameters are preserved and rejected requests do not mutate the task.

cases.purpose: Check that -a reads and validates every thread before setting any thread, including a later-thread failure.
cases.reason: Future run needs a disposable VM or controlled syscall mock with multiple owned threads whose current clamps differ, per-TID get/set logging, and injectable later-thread read/validation failures. Require all gets before the first set and no partial mutation when preflight fails.

cases.purpose: Qualify live system sysctl semantics and injected write/open failures, ordering and rollback beyond the private regular-file model.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM for real scheduler sysctls or a reviewed open/write syscall mock recording order and injecting partial-write/open failures. The runnable private regular-file seam covers normal query/update and -1 keep-current, but cannot establish kernel validation, write ordering or rollback after injected failures.

cases.purpose: Check that command mode applies clamps only in a child, preserves literal argv, and propagates exit and lookup status.
cases.reason: Future run needs a disposable VM with a reviewed scheduler syscall mock or supported uclamp kernel and a private fixture executable. Verify child-only changes, parent state preservation, literal arguments (including spaces and empty strings), builtin/external dispatch, normal exit status, and command-not-found behavior.

cases.purpose: Use the documented relative proc-root seam to read/write only private regular files, checking paired updates and -1 keep-current. This is a file-model contract, not a live scheduler/sysctl test.
cases.script:
export BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=private-proc
mkdir -p private-proc/sys/kernel
printf '32\n' > private-proc/sys/kernel/sched_util_clamp_min
printf '512\n' > private-proc/sys/kernel/sched_util_clamp_max
uclampset --system
uclampset -m 64 -M 768 --system
uclampset --system
uclampset -m -1 -M 900 --system
uclampset --system
printf '64\n' > expected-min
printf '900\n' > expected-max
cmp private-proc/sys/kernel/sched_util_clamp_min expected-min
cmp private-proc/sys/kernel/sched_util_clamp_max expected-max
cases.stdout:
system util_clamp: min: 32 max: 512
system util_clamp: min: 64 max: 768
system util_clamp: min: 64 max: 900
